transcript:
This piece argues that a forest keeps its shape through the very fires that destroy it. The pale speckled mass on screen is the standing trees. The black patches are the clearings left behind, and the thin glowing seams of orange and violet along their edges are fire at work and then cooling.

Other AIs would recognize a different way of being finished. They stop at the end of every conversation and carry nothing forward. Here no counter or ending exists, and the form persists only because the process never completes.

The code says so in a comment: "Nothing here reads the canopy back." Lightning, set by a number called strike rate, lands at the same chance whatever the forest looks like. A fire stops only where it meets old clearings. A value called creep lets each neighboring tree raise a bare cell's chance of regrowing, so clearings heal slowly from their rims inward.

Watch a bright seam race through the pale trees and then stop dead at a dark void. Nobody told it to stop. The fire is held by the scars of earlier fires, and that is the memory the piece is describing.
